_comment: Single source of truth for statutory fees and caps cited across the site. Every figure here is verified against a primary source. If a fee changes, change it HERE and re-run scripts/check_statutory_fees.py to find every page that still carries the old value. Do not hard-code these numbers into new pages without adding them here first.
_verified_by: Claude Code, against gov.uk / legislation.gov.uk primary sources

winding_up_petition_court_fee.description: Court fee for entering a winding-up petition (companies only).

winding_up_petition_deposit.description: Petition deposit payable to the Insolvency Service on a winding-up petition (other than under s.124A). Superseded list added 2026-08-09 after £2,400 was found on a live page; the entry previously had no superseded values, so no amount of drift was detectable.

strike_off_ds01_online.description: Companies House fee to apply for voluntary strike-off (DS01) online.

strike_off_ds01_paper.description: Companies House fee to apply for voluntary strike-off (DS01) by paper.

statutory_weekly_pay_cap.description: Statutory weekly pay cap used for redundancy, arrears, notice and holiday pay claims. Effective 6 April 2026.

statutory_redundancy_maximum.description: Maximum statutory redundancy payment (£751 weekly cap x 30 weeks).
statutory_redundancy_maximum.source_name: Derived from the statutory weekly pay cap

_commercial_fees_comment: NOT statutory. These are Company Debt's own prices, so they are not verifiable against gov.uk. They are here because they drifted just as badly: the CVL fee was published as £4,000-£6,000 on four pages and £4,000-£7,000 on another, and disbursements as both £500-£1,000 and £500-£1,500. Owner set the canonical values on 2026-07-14.

cvl_practitioner_fee.description: Company Debt CVL practitioner fee, plus VAT, standard fixed fee for a straightforward case. Changed from a £4,000-£7,000 range to a flat £3,500 on 2026-07-15 (owner). Note: £4,000-£5,000 is NOT a drift pattern here - it is the current all-in figure (see cvl_all_in). Drift regex widened 2026-07-15 to also catch the '£4-£7k' shorthand range that appeared on some pages. Widened 2026-08-09: the flat-fee change left bare-figure survivors ('from around £5,000', '£5,000 or more', '£5,000 upfront', 'starts from around £5,000') on five pages that the range-only patterns could not see, plus a '£4-7k' shorthand with no second currency symbol. Bare £5,000 is gated on CVL context and excluded near CVA or administration, where it is a legitimate figure.

cvl_disbursements.description: Bond, Gazette notices, Companies House filing, statutory mailings.

cvl_all_in.description: Derived: £3,500 fixed fee + £500-£1,500 disbursements. Was £5,000-£9,000 when the fee was a £4,000-£7,000 range.

mvl_practitioner_fee.description: Company Debt MVL practitioner fee, plus VAT, standard fixed fee for a solvent company. Changed from a £2,000-£4,000 range to a flat £3,500 on 2026-07-15 (owner). Drift regex widened 2026-07-15: several MVL pages carried the fee as a £3,000-£5,000, £2,000-£5,000 or '£2-£5k' range, which the original £2,000-£4,000 pattern did not catch, so check_statutory_fees.py let them through. The new variants are deliberately gated to MVL/IP-fee context, because a bare £2,000-£5,000 or £3,000-£5,000 range also legitimately describes PGI premiums, pre-pack evaluator fees and legal-challenge costs - a context-free pattern flagged those as false positives, and a guard that cries wolf gets ignored.

badr_rate.description: Business Asset Disposal Relief CGT rate on qualifying gains within the £1m lifetime limit. 10% until 5 April 2025, 14% for 2025/26, 18% for disposals on or after 6 April 2026. Added 2026-08-09: three pages still said 10%, understating the tax by eight points on exactly the MVL-versus-dissolution decision they exist to inform, while two other pages already said 18%. A partial migration nothing was checking. Historical framing ('risen from 14%', 'before that, 10%') is allowed by the HISTORICAL guard in the checker.

preferential_wages_limit.description: Per-employee limit on preferential status for arrears of wages in an insolvency.

prohibited_name_period_years.description: Section 216 IA 1986 restriction on re-using a liquidated company's name (or a confusingly similar one) without court permission.

disqualification_range_years.description: Director disqualification order length under CDDA 1986 s.6 following a conduct report.

official_cvl_count_2025.description: Registered company insolvencies in England and Wales, 2025, and the CVL share of them. The four years to 2025 contain the four highest annual CVL totals since the series began in 1960.
official_cvl_count_2025.source_name: The Insolvency Service, Company Insolvency Statistics

creditor_decision_and_filing_deadlines.description: The special resolution to wind up must be filed at Companies House within 15 days of being passed, and advertised in The Gazette within 14 days of being passed. This is separate from the creditor decision procedure, under which creditors are given notice of the liquidator-appointment decision.

_banned_claims._comment: Figures that must NOT appear anywhere on the site. Each was traced to an unverifiable origin. scripts/check_statutory_fees.py fails any page containing them.

director_redundancy_average._note: Regex, not literals: the claim appears in several phrasings and a literal list missed most of them. Two tiers, because £9,000 also legitimately appears as the top of the CVL all-in cost range (£5,000 to £9,000). banned_patterns are unambiguous and fire anywhere. banned_patterns_in_context are loose and only fire near a redundancy/claim word, so they do not flag a genuine cost figure.
director_redundancy_average.reason: Presented as an average successful director redundancy claim, but not supported by the cited gov.uk guidance. Traced to editorial-os/17-audience-and-persona.md and to Gemini research output, not to Company Debt caseload. Owner confirmed on 2026-07-14 that the firm cannot stand behind it.
director_redundancy_average.use_instead: The statutory calculation method (age, length of service, weekly pay), the £751 weekly cap, the £22,530 maximum, and a link to https://www.gov.uk/calculate-your-redundancy-pay so the reader gets their own figure.
